sentences.text: This petition is filed by the L.R's of one deceased Sri. Shubham Mahadev Patil under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ in respect of death of one Shubham Mahadev Patil in Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 01.07.2023 at about 7.00 a.m he was proceeding in a Trailer Container bearing Reg.No.NL01AD1875 as a cleaner and the said vehicle was driven by its driver by name Mahadev Manohar Waghe from Tumkur towards Bangalore side in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations, while so proceeding he reached Near T.Beguru, infront of TCI Godown, Bengaluru.

Due to the negligent driving, the driver lost control over the vehicle and dashed to the road center median and jumped to either side of the road and dashed against the opposite coming Trailer vehicle bearing No.KA01AK0559 and caused accident.
Consequent to (SCCH12) 3 MVC No.5519/2023 which, he succumbed to the fatal injuries and died on the spot.
Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Govt. hospital, Nelamangala wherein.
Post mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the claimants.
The petitioners have shifted the dead body to their residence by hiring a vehicle and have performed funeral and obsequies ceremonies by spending more than Rs.1,00,000/.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged 19 years at the time of death.
He was working as 'Cleaner' in a Trailer Container, and earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
He was contributing his entire income to the maintenance of his family members.
Since the deceased was only earning member of the family the petitioners were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the untimely death of the deceased the petitioner no.1 and 2 are the parents of deceased and have lost love and affection and caring son.

The accident is purely due to the rash and negligent manner of driving of the Trailer Container bearing Reg.No.NL01 AD1875 by its driver and in this connection the jurisdictional Nelamangala Traffic police, have filed charge sheet against the said driver in Crime 281/2023 for the offence P/u/S 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.

The 1st respondent is the R.C. owner of Trailer Container bearing Reg.No.NL01 AD1875 and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of said Trailer container are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
On all these grounds petitioners prayed to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ with costs and interest in the above case.
On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
Respondent no.2 insurance company appeared through its counsel and have filed written statement contending that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
This respondent denies their liability in case the petitioner establishes the policy that the owner of the vehicle has failed to intimate this respondent about the accident.

That the owner has failed to Mahadev Ananda Patil vs Sandeep Logistics on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119666132/
2 produce the insurer the relevant documents such as RC, FC DL etc to establish that the vehicle was road worthy and was ridden by a rider holding a valid and effective driving license to rider the specified class of vehicle.

sentences.text: That in case the petitioner established the issuance of policy to the Trailer container bearing reg.no. NL01AD1875 the liability to indemnification is subject to Section 64 VB of the Insurance Act.
This respondent seeks protection under Section 147 and 149(2) of M.V.Act.

As per section 134 of M.V.Act it is mandatory duty of the insured 1st respondent to furnish the particulars of policy, date time and place of accident, particulars of damages/injuries and the name of the driver and his driving license particulars, but the insured has not complied with statutory demand.
The concerned police authorities have not complied the provisions of Section 158(6) of M.V.Act.

That the Trailer container bearing reg.no. NL01AD 1875 was not at all involved in the accident and the driver of the alleged vehicle was no way related in the alleged accident as on the date of the accident.

The jurisdictional police have filed a false charge sheet against the driver of the Trailer (SCCH12) 5 MVC No.5519/2023 container bearing reg.no. NL01AD1875 colluding with the claimant and owner of the vehicle.

That the driver of the Trailer container bearing reg.no. Further he denied the age,
income, occupation and also denied the manner of accident and involvement of the vehicle.
He sought permission to defend the claim petition on all grounds under Section 170 of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further he contended that, the amount claimed as compensation is baseless, speculative,
imaginary and exorbitant and this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessors inoffice has framed following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners proves that on 01.07.2023 at 7.00 am, one Shubham Mahadev Patil was traveling in a Trailer container bearing reg.no. NL01AD1875 as cleaner and said vehicle was driven by one Mahadev Manohar Waghe from Tumkur towards Bengaluru in rash and negligent manner and when it reached near T.Begut in front of TCI Godown Bengaluru, driver of the said vehicle lost control and dashed against the road divider and dashed against another trailer vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA01AK0559 (SCCH12) 6 MVC No.5519/2023 coming from opposite direction and caused accident, due to the impact said Shubham Mahadev Patil sustained injuries and died on the spot.?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove that the driver of Trailer container bearing reg.no. NL 01AD 1875 was having DL and valid insurance at the time of accident as alleged?

3. Whether the petitioners proves the age, occupation, income of deceased and their permanent dependency on him?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, by whom and what is the quantum?
5.
What Order or Award?

6. Heard learned counsel for petitioner and perused records.
7.

On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Affirmative, Issue No.3: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.4: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.5: As per final order,
for the following;
 (SCCH12) 7 MVC No.5519/2023  REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : To prove the case of petitioners, that driver of Trailer container bearing reg.no.NL01AD1875 was negligent, 2nd petitioner got examined as P.W.1 and reiterated petition averments in her chief examination affidavit.

She has produced FIR, first information, mahazar, rough sketch, IMV, P.M and inquest report, MLC intimation by the Manasvi hospital Nelamangala to police, copy of final report and death certificate of the Shubam Mahadev Patil at Ex.P.1 to 9 and 13 respectively.
As per the death certificate Shubam expired on 01.07.2023 and petitioners are his parents.
As per the post mortem report, death of Shubam expired due to hypovulnoric shock due to injury to brain and long bones due to road traffic accident.

As per the FIR one Siddarama, who is cleaner in vehicle KA01AK 0559 has given first information to police stating that he was traveling as cleaner in the aforesaid vehicle and going towards Hosapete for the purpose of loading that he was sitting in the cabin of the Trailer container bearing reg.no. KA01AK0559 and when himself and his driver reached near ParleG factory at 6.00am on NH48, BengaluruTumkur road, one vehicle Trailer container bearing reg.no. NL01AD1875 came in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle hit the median and entered the other side road and dashed against the vehicle in which this informant was traveling.
The first informant and his driver sustained injuries and also that in the vehicle No. NL01AD1875 one of the cleaners expired and another got injured, even driver of the said vehicle got injured.

On the basis of this information given by the first informant,
Nelamangala Police have registered FIR in Crime No.281/2022 for the offence p/u/s 279, 337 and 338 of IPC against the driver of Trailer container bearing reg.no. NL01AD1875.
After investigation final report is filed against the same driver as per Ex.P.9 charge sheet.

There is sketch produced at Ex.P.4 shows that,the Trailer container bearing reg.no. NL01AD1875 has crossed Mahadev Ananda Patil vs Sandeep Logistics on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119666132/
4 the median and came to the opposite road and dashed against another Trailer container.

sentences.text: That clearly shows that the driver of said vehicle was negligent in driving the vehicle.
As per IMV report produced at Ex.P.5 accident was not due to any mechanical defect in the vehicle.
As such, the driver of the said vehicle is negligent in driving the same.
9. In the cross examination of P.W.1 who is not an eye witness to the incident.
It is suggested that a false case is filed against the opponent vehicle she denied the same.
There is no respondent side evidence.

Therefore, on the basis of materials available on record, it is clear that the driver of Trailer container bearing reg.no. NL01AD1875 was negligent and due to the accident caused by him the cleaner by name Shubam Mahadev Patil expired.
Accordingly, I answer this issue No. 1 in the Affirmative.
10. ISSUE NO.2:

The 2nd respondent contended that the driver of Trailer container bearing reg.no.
NL01AD1875 was not having valid driving licence at the time of accident.

To prove the same respondent evidence is not led, but since the burden (SCCH12) 9 MVC No.5519/2023 is on the petitioner to prove the D.L was existing at the time of accident petitioner has produced the final report at Ex.P.9.
In the said final report there is no mention about not having D.L by the driver.
To say that incorrect final report is filed, respondent has not led any evidence are not proved that driver had no D.L.
Therefore, what is mentioned in the final report deserved to be accepted in the absence of any contra evidence.
Hence, it is held that the petitioners have proved that the driver Trailer container bearing reg.no. NL01AD1875 was having valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
In respect of insurance, in written statement 2nd respondent denies the existence of police, but in the petitioner it is mentioned that from 27.02.2023 till 26.02.2024 there was insurance.
There is no mention in the final report in respect of the fact that not having insurance as on the date of accident.
Further in the records there is copy of the insurance copy available which shows that the policy was valid with ICICI Lombard Company from 27.02.2023 to 26.02.2024.
Accident took place on 01.07.2023 which is within the period of insurance.
Hence, petitioners have proved this issue.
Accordingly, I hold this issue in the Affirmative.
11. ISSUE No.3:
To prove the age of the deceased petitioners mentioned in the petition that he was aged 19 years at the time of accident.
In Ex.P.12 aadhaar card is produced which shows he was born on 18.05.2004.
As on the date of accident i.e., 01.07.2023 he was aged 19 years.
Even the age of the deceased is not disputed in the cross examination of P.W., (SCCH12) 10 MVC No.5519/2023 therefore it is considered that he was aged about 29 years at the time of accident.
In the records it is mentioned that he was Cleaner.
The occupation of deceased is not disputed in the cross examination of P.W.1.
Further petitioners being parents are dependents on the deceased.

12. In respect of income it is stated in the petition that the deceased was cleaner and was earning Rs.
20,000/ per month.
Under whom he was working is not stated.
Nor the documentary evidence regarding income proof is produced.
Therefore, notional income as to be gathered.
He was cleaner is not disputed.

Having regard to the year of accident being 2023 and he was aged 19 years, this court is of the opinion that if the notional income of Rs. 15,000/ per month is considered, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence it is held that monthly income of the deceased was Rs. 15,000/ per month.
Accordingly, I hold this issue Partly in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: ISSUE No.4:
in view of above reasons, petitioners re entitled for compensation.
Since negligence is proved, it is 1 st respondent who is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
In view of valid in insurance policy as on the date of accident, 2nd respondent has to indemnify the insured.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
14. Loss of dependency :
As per finding to Issue no.3, petitioners are held to be dependents on the deceased.
As per the Praney Sethi case future prospects of the deceased will have to be added to the monthly income.
In case of self employed (SCCH12) 11 MVC No.5519/2023 40% of the income has to be added to the monthly income to the age group below 40 years.
Age of the deceased in this case is 19 years.

Therefore, in the present case the monthly income of deceased is Rs.15,000/ + 6,000/
= Rs.21,000/.
Further deceased being bachelor having 2 dependents 1/2 of his income shall be deducted towards his personal expenses.

As such, loss of dependency of the petitioners due to the death of their family member is Rs.22,68,000/
15.
Loss of love and affection:
Petitioners being L.R's of the deceased have lost the love and affection of their son due to his death in the accident.
Therefore, for loss of love and affection compensation has to be granted.

There is no hard and fast rule in respect of measuring love and affection but, in the opinion of this court if amount of Rs.50,000/ is awarded for loss of love and affection, the interest of justice would be met.
Accordingly, amount of Rs.50,000/ is awarded.
16. Loss of Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses:

As per the judgment in Praney Sethi's case, the quantum of compensation for Loss of Consortium is fixed @ Rs.40,000/ and loss of estate and funeral expenses is fixed @ (SCCH12) 12 MVC No.5519/2023 Rs.15,000/ respectively and it is revisable at 10% every 3 years.
As such, under the head of loss of estate Rs.18,000/, for funeral expenses Rs.18,000/ and for loss of consortium Rs.48,000/ each to petitioner no.1 and 2 is awarded.

Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation as under:
Sl.No. Particulars of Heads Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Dependency : 22,68,000 /
2. Loss of love & affection : 50,000/
3. Loss of Consortium to : 88,000/ petitioner no.1 &2 ( Rs.48,000/ each)
4. Loss of Estate : 18,000/

sentences.text: Therefore, I hold that the petitioners are entitled for a compensation of Rs.24,42,000 /.
Hence, I answer this Issue in "Partly Affirmative".
17. ISSUE No.5:
Petitioners have sought for compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ in respect of death of Shubham patil in road traffic accident.
They have not claimed any rate of interest on the compensation amount.
But as per the settled law, the interest that could be awarded on the compensation is only 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till the payment.

Hence, in view of above reasons petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.24,42,000 / with interest @ 6%
p.a from the date of petition till the date of payment.
1st and 2 petitioners (SCCH12) 13 MVC No.5519/2023 being parents of the deceased are entitled to 50% each in the total compensation.

In such apportionment 50% amount of petitioner no.1 and 2 shall be ordered to be kept in F.D in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 50% shall be ordered to be released in their favour.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.24,42,000/ with interest @ 6%
p.a. on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment from respondents No.1 and 2.
In view of valid insurance policy, respondent no.2 shall indemnify the insured and hereby directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this court within 2 months from the date of this order.
Out of the total compensation amount with cost and interest awarded to the petitioners, petitioner no.1 and 2 are entitled to 50% each in the total compensation.
(SCCH12) 14 MVC No.5519/2023 Out of compensation amount with cost and interest awarded to the petitioner no.1 and 2, 50% is ordered to be released in their favour and remaining 50% is ordered to be deposited as FD in the name of petitioner no.1 and 2 in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years with liberty to withdraw the periodical accrued interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Award be drawn accordingly.
